title: Privileged representational axes in biological and artificial neural networks
title_zh: 生物与人工神经网络中的特权表征轴
abstract: How do neurons code information? Recent work emphasizes the geometry and information content of population codes, using measures that are blind to the native tunings (or ‘axes’) of neural responses. But might these representational axes matter, with some privileged systematically over others? We developed methods to test for alignment of neural tuning across brains and deep convolutional neural networks (DCNNs). Across both vision and audition, both brains and DCNNs consistently favoured certain axes for representing the natural world. Moreover, the representational axes of DCNNs trained on natural inputs were aligned to those in perceptual cortices, such that axis-sensitive model–brain similarity metrics better differentiated competing models of biological sensory systems. We further show that coding schemes that privilege certain axes can facilitate task performance, reduce downstream wiring costs and improve generalization. These results motivate a new framework for understanding neural tuning in biological and artificial networks and its computational benefits. Khosla et al. show that both brains and neural networks consistently favoured certain axes for representing the natural world.
abstract_zh: 神经元如何编码信息？最近的研究强调了群体编码的几何结构和信息含量，使用的指标对神经反应的原生调谐（或‘轴’）视而不见。但这些表征轴是否重要，是否存在系统偏向于某些轴？我们开发了测试跨大脑和深度卷积神经网络（DCNN）调谐对齐的方法。在视觉和听觉中，大脑和DCNN都一致偏向于代表自然世界的特定轴。此外，训练于自然输入的DCNN的表征轴与感觉皮层的轴一致对齐，这种轴敏感的模型-大脑相似度指标能更好地区分生物感觉系统的竞争模型。我们进一步表明，优先考虑特定轴的编码方案可以促进任务表现，降低下游布线成本并提高泛化能力。这些结果激发了一个新的框架，用于理解生物和人工网络中的神经调谐及其计算优势。Khosla等人表明，大脑和神经网络在代表自然世界时一致偏向于某些轴。
